records.source: Τὸν μὲν πρῶτον λόγον ἐποιησάμην περὶ πάντων, ὦ Θεόφιλε, ὧν ἤρξατο ὁ Ἰησοῦς ποιεῖν τε καὶ διδάσκειν ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας ἐντειλάμενος τοῖς ἀποστόλοις διὰ πνεύματος ἁγίου οὓς ἐξελέξατο ἀνελήμφθη·
records.gloss: The indeed first account I made concerning all [things], O Theophilus, which began the Jesus both to do and to teach, \v 2 until which day, having given orders to the apostles through Spirit Holy whom he chose, he was taken up.
pieces: Theophilus, the first book I composed told of all that Jesus began both to do and to teach,
until the day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was taken up. Before that, through the Holy Spirit, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had given orders to the apostles {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had chosen.

L.1: The first account I made, O Theophilus, [was] about all that Jesus began both to do and to teach,
L.2: until the day when, having given orders through [the] Holy Spirit to the apostles whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had chosen, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was taken up.

R.1: Dear Theophilus, my first book was about everything Jesus began to do and to teach.
R.2: It went on until the day God took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up to heaven. Before {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave orders to the apostles {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had chosen. He did this through the Holy Spirit.

decisions.choice: the first account: Luke's earlier book, the Gospel
alternatives: the first of several works still to come
decisions.reason: Luke's Gospel is also written to Theophilus (Luke 1:1-4), and it ends where this book begins, with Jesus taken up near Bethany (Luke 24:50-51). The word for "account" can mean a written work.

decisions.choice: Theophilus: a real person to whom the work is addressed
alternatives: a name for every reader who loves God
decisions.reason: The name means "loved by God" or "friend of God", and some have read it as a name for any believer. But it was an ordinary name of the time, and in Luke 1:3 he is addressed with a title of honor, as a real person would be.

decisions.choice: began to do and to teach: what Jesus started in the Gospel goes on in this book
alternatives: "began" adds nothing: all that Jesus did and taught
decisions.reason: Greek can use "began" with little weight. But Acts goes on to tell what the risen Jesus does through his apostles and the Spirit (2:33, 9:5), so the word likely points forward.

decisions.choice: through the Holy Spirit goes with "having given orders"
alternatives: through the Holy Spirit goes with "whom he had chosen"
decisions.reason: The Greek order allows either. Most naturally, the phrase tells how Jesus gave his orders; Luke 4:1 and 4:14 show Jesus acting in the Spirit's power. The choosing of the Twelve was also done after prayer (Luke 6:12-13).

decisions.choice: was taken up: Jesus taken up into heaven, told in 1:9-11
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of Jesus going up into heaven in 1:11 and 1:22. The passive leaves God as the one who takes him up.

decisions.choice: Dear Theophilus; God took him up to heaven
alternatives: O Theophilus; he was taken up
decisions.reason: English does not use "O" to address someone in a letter, so Readable says "Dear". It names God as the one who acts in the passive verb, and says where Jesus was taken, which the meaning note explains.

records.heading: Waiting for the promise of the Father

records.source: οἷς καὶ παρέστησεν ἑαυτὸν ζῶντα μετὰ τὸ παθεῖν αὐτὸν ἐν πολλοῖς τεκμηρίοις, δι’ ἡμερῶν τεσσεράκοντα ὀπτανόμενος αὐτοῖς καὶ λέγων τὰ περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ·
records.gloss: To whom also he presented himself living after the to suffer him by many proofs, through days forty being seen by them and speaking the things concerning the kingdom of the God.
pieces: To them as well {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had shown {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} alive after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} suffered, with many clear proofs, as for forty days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} let them see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and told them about the kingdom of God.

L.3: To them also {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} presented {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} alive after {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} suffering by many convincing proofs, appearing to them through forty days and speaking the things concerning the kingdom of God.

R.3: After Jesus had suffered and died, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed the apostles that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was alive again. He gave them many proofs that left no room for doubt. For forty days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} kept appearing to them and talking with them about God's kingdom.

decisions.choice: convincing proofs: signs that settle the matter
decisions.reason: The word was used for evidence that decides a question beyond doubt. Luke 24:36-43 shows such proofs: the risen Jesus is touched, and eats in front of them.

decisions.choice: after his suffering: after his death on the cross
alternatives: the pain before his death only
decisions.reason: In Luke and Acts, "suffer" said of the Messiah takes in his death (Luke 24:26, 24:46; Acts 3:18).

decisions.choice: through forty days: he appeared again and again over that time
alternatives: he stayed with them without a break for forty days
decisions.reason: The participle "being seen" describes appearances that came and went. In 13:31 Paul says he "appeared for many days" to those who came up with him from Galilee.

decisions.choice: the kingdom of God: God's rule, the theme that opens and closes Acts
decisions.reason: Acts ends with Paul proclaiming the kingdom of God in Rome (28:31). The apostles' question in 1:6 shows they heard him speaking of God's promised reign.

decisions.choice: Jesus; the apostles; suffered and died
alternatives: he; to them; after his suffering
decisions.reason: Readable names the people the pronouns point to, and says that the suffering included his death, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: καὶ συναλιζόμενος παρήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων μὴ χωρίζεσθαι, ἀλλὰ περιμένειν τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ πατρὸς ἣν ἠκούσατέ μου·
records.gloss: And eating together he ordered them from Jerusalem not to depart, but to wait for the promise of the Father which you heard of me.
pieces: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shared a meal with them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} charged them not to go away from Jerusalem but to wait there for what the Father had promised: "the promise you heard about from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.4: And while eating together [with them], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ordered them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to wait for the promise of the Father, "which you heard from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.4: While {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was eating a meal with them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them, "Do not leave Jerusalem. Stay here and wait for what the Father promised to send. I have told you about this.

decisions.choice: eating together: sharing a meal with them
decisions.reason: The word is rare. It can be read as "sharing salt", that is, eating together, and Acts 10:41 says the apostles "ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead" (also Luke 24:41-43). A very similar word means "to stay with", and others take it as "assembling".

decisions.choice: which you heard from me: Luke slips from reporting Jesus's words into quoting them
decisions.reason: The sentence begins as reported speech ("he ordered them") and moves to Jesus's own words, so "me" is Jesus. Greek writers often slide from one to the other. The quotation runs to the end of 1:5.

decisions.choice: the promise of the Father: the Holy Spirit, whom the Father promised to give
decisions.reason: 1:5 names what is promised, and Peter says in 2:33 that Jesus received "the promise of the Holy Spirit" from the Father and poured it out. In Luke 24:49 Jesus says "I am sending the promise of my Father upon you".

decisions.choice: the quotation opens at "which you heard" (B), and at the order not to leave (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced opens the quotation where the Greek turns to Jesus's own words. Readable turns the whole order into direct speech, which is easier to follow.

decisions.choice: what the Father promised to send
decisions.reason: "To send" makes the promise concrete: the Father is sending the Spirit (Luke 24:49).

records.source: ὅτι Ἰωάννης μὲν ἐβάπτισεν ὕδατι, ὑμεῖς δὲ ἐν πνεύματι βαπτισθήσεσθε ἁγίῳ οὐ μετὰ πολλὰς ταύτας ἡμέρας.
records.gloss: For John indeed baptized with water, you but in Spirit will be baptized Holy not after many these days.
pieces: For John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit before many days have passed."

L.5: For John baptized with water, but you will be baptized in [the] Holy Spirit not many days after these."

R.5: John baptized people with water. But in only a few days, God will baptize you with the Holy Spirit."

decisions.choice: John's own words, now spoken by Jesus: water, then the Spirit
decisions.reason: John the Baptist said he baptized with water but the one coming after him would baptize with the Holy Spirit (Luke 3:16). Peter recalls this saying of Jesus in 11:16.

decisions.choice: in the Holy Spirit: the Spirit is poured out like the water they are dipped in
alternatives: by the Holy Spirit as the one who baptizes
decisions.reason: The phrase stands next to "with water" and works the same way: the Spirit is what they will be immersed in. In 2:17-18, 2:33 the Spirit is "poured out".

decisions.choice: not many days after these: soon
decisions.reason: Greek often says "not many" for "few". The Spirit comes at Pentecost (2:1), about ten days after the forty days of 1:3.

decisions.choice: God will baptize you
decisions.reason: Readable names the one who acts in the passive verb. Peter says in 2:33 that Jesus, having received the Spirit from the Father, poured it out; naming God keeps to what the Greek implies without choosing between them.

records.source: Οἱ μὲν οὖν συνελθόντες ἠρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Κύριε, εἰ ἐν τῷ χρόνῳ τούτῳ ἀποκαθιστάνεις τὴν βασιλείαν τῷ Ἰσραήλ;
records.gloss: Those indeed therefore having come together were asking him saying, Lord, if at the time this you are restoring the kingdom to the Israel?
pieces: When they had gathered, they kept asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, is this the time when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will restore the kingdom to Israel?"

L.6: So those who had come together were asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Lord, at this time are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} restoring the kingdom to Israel?"

R.6: So when the apostles met with Jesus, they asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, is this the time {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will give the kingdom back to Israel?"

decisions.choice: those who had come together: the apostles, gathered with Jesus
decisions.reason: "So" ties the question to what Jesus has just said about the Spirit. The place seems to be the Mount of Olives, from which they return in 1:12.

decisions.choice: "if" here opens a direct question
decisions.reason: In the Greek of this time "if" can introduce a direct question, as in Luke 13:23 and Acts 19:2.

decisions.choice: restore the kingdom to Israel: give Israel back its own kingdom under God's king
decisions.reason: The hope is for the throne of David to be set up again (Luke 1:32-33) and Israel set free (Luke 24:21). Jesus does not deny the hope; he refuses to give a date (1:7) and turns them to their task (1:8).

decisions.choice: were asking: they asked more than once, or pressed the question
decisions.reason: The tense describes an ongoing action.

decisions.choice: the apostles met with Jesus; give the kingdom back
alternatives: those who had come together; restore the kingdom
decisions.reason: Readable names those present and says "restore" in common words.

records.heading: Jesus is taken up

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Οὐχ ὑμῶν ἐστιν γνῶναι χρόνους ἢ καιροὺς οὓς ὁ πατὴρ ἔθετο ἐν τῇ ἰδίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ, ἀλλὰ λήμψεσθε δύναμιν ἐπελθόντος τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἔσεσθέ μου μάρτυρες ἔν τε Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ ἐν πάσῃ τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ καὶ Σαμαρείᾳ καὶ ἕως ἐσχάτου τῆς γῆς.
records.gloss: He said but to them, Not yours it is to know times or seasons which the Father set in the own authority, \v 8 but you will receive power having come the Holy Spirit upon you, and you will be of me witnesses in both Jerusalem and in all the Judea and Samaria and to [the] end of the earth.
pieces: He answered them, "Times and seasons that the Father has fixed by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own authority are not yours to know.

But when the Holy Spirit comes upon you, you will receive power, and you will bear witness to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in Jerusalem, through all Judea and Samaria, and out to the farthest end of the earth."

L.7: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "It is not yours to know times or seasons which the Father has set by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own authority,
L.8: but you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witnesses both in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to [the] end of the earth."

R.7: Jesus said to them, "Those times and dates are not for you to know. The Father has set them, and they are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} to decide.
R.8: But the Holy Spirit will come on you, and you will receive power. Then you will tell people about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You will tell them in Jerusalem, in all of Judea and Samaria, and in the farthest places on earth."

decisions.choice: times or seasons: how long, and at what set moment
alternatives: two words for the same thing
decisions.reason: The first word is time as a span, the second a fitting or appointed time. Together they mean "when", as in 1 Thessalonians 5:1.

decisions.choice: but: in place of knowing the date, they are given power for a task
decisions.reason: "But" turns from what is not theirs (the timing) to what will be theirs (power from the Spirit).

decisions.choice: witnesses: people who saw and now tell what they saw
alternatives: martyrs, people who die for their faith
decisions.reason: In Acts a witness has seen the risen Jesus and speaks of it (1:22, 2:32, 10:39-41). The later sense "martyr" grew from this word, but it is not the meaning here.

decisions.choice: my witnesses: they belong to Jesus and speak about him
alternatives: only witnesses who belong to him
decisions.reason: The Greek "of me" can mean either; both are true in Acts, where the apostles are sent by Jesus and speak of him.

decisions.choice: to the end of the earth: the words of Isaiah 49:6, and the path Acts follows
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 49:6 God's servant is made a light for the nations, "that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth"; Paul quotes it in 13:47. Acts tells the story in this order: Jerusalem (chapters 1-7), Judea and Samaria (8-9), then the nations as far as Rome.

decisions.choice: you will bear witness to me
decisions.reason: Balanced says it with a verb, which keeps both senses of "of me": they are his, and they speak of him.

decisions.choice: you will tell people about me; they are his to decide
alternatives: you will be my witnesses; by his own authority
decisions.reason: Readable says what a witness does, and says "authority" in plain words.

records.source: καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν βλεπόντων αὐτῶν ἐπήρθη καὶ νεφέλη ὑπέλαβεν αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And these things having said, watching them, he was lifted up, and a cloud took up him from the eyes of them.
pieces: With these words said, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was lifted up as they watched, and a cloud received {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so that their eyes could no longer see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.9: And having said these things, as they were watching, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was lifted up, and a cloud took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up from their eyes.

R.9: After Jesus said this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was lifted up into the sky while they watched. Then a cloud covered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they could not see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} anymore.

decisions.choice: took him up: the cloud received him and bore him out of sight
decisions.reason: The verb means to take up from beneath, or to receive. The cloud is more than a curtain: it carries him away (compare 1:11, "taken up").

decisions.choice: the cloud: a sign of God's presence
decisions.reason: A cloud marks God's presence at Sinai and over the tent (Exodus 19:9, 40:34) and at Jesus's transfiguration (Luke 9:34-35). In Daniel 7:13 one like a son of man comes with the clouds of heaven to God, and Jesus says he will come back "in a cloud" (Luke 21:27).

decisions.choice: was lifted up: God lifted him
alternatives: he rose by his own act
decisions.reason: The passive leaves God as the one who acts, as in 1:2 and 1:11.

decisions.choice: into the sky
decisions.reason: Readable says where he was lifted, as 1:10 does.

records.source: καὶ ὡς ἀτενίζοντες ἦσαν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν πορευομένου αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο παρειστήκεισαν αὐτοῖς ἐν ἐσθήσεσι λευκαῖς, οἳ καὶ εἶπαν· Ἄνδρες Γαλιλαῖοι, τί ἑστήκατε βλέποντες εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν;
records.gloss: And as gazing they were into the sky, going him, and look, men two stood by them in clothes white, \v 11 who also said, Men Galileans, why do you stand looking into the sky?
pieces: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went, they kept their eyes fixed on the sky, and all at once two men dressed in white were there beside them.
"Men of Galilee," they said, "why stand there gazing up at the sky?

L.10: And as they were gazing into the sky while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going, then look, two men stood beside them in white clothing,
L.11: who also said, "Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into the sky?

R.10: The apostles were still staring at the sky as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went away. Then suddenly two men wearing white clothes were standing next to them.
R.11: They said, "Men from Galilee, why are you standing here looking at the sky?

decisions.choice: two men in white: messengers from God, angels
decisions.reason: Luke tells of "two men" in dazzling clothes at the empty tomb (Luke 24:4), whom the women later call angels (Luke 24:23). White clothing marks heavenly beings (Luke 9:29-30).

decisions.choice: the sky: the word means both sky and heaven
alternatives: heaven, as a place beyond the sky
decisions.reason: They are looking up at the sky where he went; the same word is "heaven" in 1:11, where he has gone. Greek has one word for both.

decisions.choice: look: a word that points to something sudden
decisions.reason: The word calls attention to what comes next, here the men who are suddenly there.

decisions.choice: men of Galilee: the apostles, who came from Galilee
decisions.reason: Jesus called his first followers in Galilee (Luke 5:1-11). Galileans could be known by their speech (Mark 14:70).

decisions.choice: look (L); all at once (B); suddenly (R)
decisions.reason: Modern English does not say "behold". Literal keeps a word that points; Balanced and Readable show the surprise in the wording.

decisions.choice: the apostles
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are.

records.source: οὗτος ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὁ ἀναλημφθεὶς ἀφ’ ὑμῶν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν οὕτως ἐλεύσεται ὃν τρόπον ἐθεάσασθε αὐτὸν πορευόμενον εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν.
records.gloss: This the Jesus the having been taken up from you into the heaven so will come in which manner you saw him going into the heaven.
pieces: This Jesus has been taken up from you into heaven, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will come in the very way you saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} leave for heaven."

L.11: This Jesus, who has been taken up from you into heaven, will so come in the manner [in] which you saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} going into heaven."

R.11: Jesus has been taken away from you into heaven. But one day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will come back. He will come in the same way you saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} go."

decisions.choice: he will come in the same way: as he went, in a cloud and seen, he will return
alternatives: his coming in the Spirit at Pentecost
decisions.reason: He went up in a cloud while they watched (1:9); Jesus said the Son of Man would come "in a cloud with power and great glory" (Luke 21:27).

decisions.choice: this Jesus: the same person, not another
decisions.reason: The words stress that the one who returns is the Jesus they knew.

decisions.choice: one day; come back
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the coming is still future and is a return.

records.source: Τότε ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἀπὸ ὄρους τοῦ καλουμένου Ἐλαιῶνος, ὅ ἐστιν ἐγγὺς Ἰερουσαλὴμ σαββάτου ἔχον ὁδόν.
records.gloss: Then they returned to Jerusalem from mountain the called Olive Grove, which is near Jerusalem, of a Sabbath having a way.
pieces: Then they went back to Jerusalem from the hill called the Mount of Olives. It lies close to the city, {{units:about half a mile|a Sabbath day's walk}} away.

L.12: Then they returned to Jerusalem from [the] mountain called Olive Grove, which is near Jerusalem, a Sabbath's journey away.

R.12: Then the apostles walked back to Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives. It was only {{units:about half a mile|a Sabbath day's walk}} from the city.

decisions.choice: a Sabbath day's journey: the distance a Jew could walk on the Sabbath, about 2,000 cubits
decisions.reason: Jewish teachers set this limit from Exodus 16:29 and the 2,000 cubits of Numbers 35:5. It is about 1,000 yards, a little over half a mile. Luke means only that the hill is close; it need not have been a Sabbath.

decisions.choice: the Mount of Olives: the ridge east of Jerusalem, across the Kidron valley
decisions.reason: Luke 24:50 places the parting near Bethany, which is on the far slope of the same ridge. Zechariah 14:4 pictures the Lord standing on this mountain on his day.

decisions.choice: about half a mile, with "a Sabbath day's walk" as the alternative
decisions.reason: A modern measure is the default and the original unit the setting, as everywhere. Literal keeps the original.

decisions.choice: the Mount of Olives
decisions.reason: The name means an olive grove. English knows the place as the Mount of Olives, as Luke himself calls it in Luke 19:29 and 22:39.

records.heading: Praying together in the upper room

records.source: καὶ ὅτε εἰσῆλθον, εἰς τὸ ὑπερῷον ἀνέβησαν οὗ ἦσαν καταμένοντες, ὅ τε Πέτρος καὶ Ἰωάννης καὶ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἀνδρέας, Φίλιππος καὶ Θωμᾶς, Βαρθολομαῖος καὶ Μαθθαῖος, Ἰάκωβος Ἁλφαίου καὶ Σίμων ὁ ζηλωτὴς καὶ Ἰούδας Ἰακώβου.
records.gloss: And when they entered, into the upper room they went up where they were staying, both Peter and John and James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James of Alphaeus and Simon the Zealot and Judas of James.
pieces: Back in the city, they climbed to the upstairs room where they had been lodging. Peter was there, with John, James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James.

L.13: And when they had entered [the city], they went up into the upper room where they were staying: Peter and John and James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James [son] of Alphaeus and Simon the Zealot and Judas [son] of James.

R.13: When they got back to the city, they went up to the room upstairs where they were staying. These were the apostles: Peter, John, James, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas the son of James.

decisions.choice: the upper room: a room on the upper floor or roof of a house
decisions.reason: Such rooms could be large (20:8-9). It may be the room of the last supper, but Luke uses a different word there (Luke 22:12), so this is not certain.

decisions.choice: the Zealot: one known for zeal
decisions.reason: Luke 6:15 also calls him "the Zealot". The word means someone zealous, for God and the law. It may also mean he had belonged to those who wanted to throw off Roman rule; the Zealot party is known by that name only some decades later.

decisions.choice: Judas of James: Judas son of James
decisions.reason: Greek often names a man by his father this way, as in "James of Alphaeus" just before. Some read "brother of James", taking him to be the author of the letter of Jude, who calls himself "brother of James" (Jude 1). He is not Judas Iscariot (John 14:22).

decisions.choice: where they were staying: the place they were living or regularly met
decisions.reason: The verb describes an ongoing stay, and 1:14 shows them continuing there.

decisions.choice: [the city]; [son]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets what English needs to make sense of the verb and of the names. Balanced and Readable say it as English would.

records.source: οὗτοι πάντες ἦσαν προσκαρτεροῦντες ὁμοθυμαδὸν τῇ προσευχῇ σὺν γυναιξὶν καὶ Μαριὰμ τῇ μητρὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ σὺν τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: These all were continuing with one mind in the prayer with women and Mary the mother of the Jesus and with the brothers of him.
pieces: All of these were devoted to prayer and of one mind in it. With them were the women, Mary the mother of Jesus, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers.

L.14: These all were devoting themselves with one mind to prayer, with [the] women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers.

R.14: They all met often and prayed with one heart. The women who had followed Jesus were with them too, and so were Mary, the mother of Jesus, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers.

decisions.choice: with one mind: united in purpose, together
decisions.reason: This is a favorite word of Luke's for the believers' unity (2:46, 4:24, 5:12).

decisions.choice: devoting themselves to prayer: they kept at it
decisions.reason: The verb means to keep at something without giving up, the same word as in 2:42. "The prayer" may include the set hours of prayer (3:1).

decisions.choice: women: the women who followed Jesus from Galilee
decisions.reason: Luke has told of women who traveled with Jesus and supported him (Luke 8:2-3) and who saw the cross, the tomb and the empty tomb (Luke 23:49, 23:55-24:10). The Greek has no article, but these are most likely the women meant.

decisions.choice: his brothers: the brothers of Jesus named in Mark 6:3
decisions.reason: Mark 6:3 names James, Joses, Judas and Simon. They did not believe in him during his ministry (John 7:5); the risen Jesus appeared to James (1 Corinthians 15:7), who later leads in Jerusalem (Acts 15:13). The word is the usual one for brothers; some Christian traditions take them to be close relatives instead.

decisions.choice: the women who had followed Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says which women, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: Καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις ἀναστὰς Πέτρος ἐν μέσῳ τῶν ἀδελφῶν εἶπεν ἦν τε ὄχλος ὀνομάτων ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ὡς ἑκατὸν εἴκοσι·
records.gloss: And in the days these having stood up Peter in middle of the brothers said (was and crowd of names at the same about 120):
pieces: In those days Peter rose to speak among the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, a crowd of about 120 people gathered in one place.

L.15: And in these days Peter stood up in [the] middle of the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} and said (and there was a crowd of names together, about 120):

R.15: During those days, the followers of Jesus met together. There were about 120 of them. Peter stood up in front of the group and spoke.

decisions.choice: the brothers: the believers, men and women
decisions.reason: "Brothers" is the common word for fellow believers in Acts. The women and Mary have just been named among them (1:14), and the group numbers 120.

decisions.choice: a crowd of names: a number of people
decisions.reason: "Names" stands for persons, as in Revelation 3:4.

decisions.choice: the number is an aside before Peter's words
decisions.reason: Luke breaks into his sentence to give the size of the group.

decisions.choice: brothers and sisters, with "brothers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word here means men and women together, as the meaning note explains, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: the followers of Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says who these brothers and sisters are. It reorders the sentence so that Peter's words follow at once.

records.heading: Matthias joins the apostles

records.source: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἔδει πληρωθῆναι τὴν γραφὴν ἣν προεῖπε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον διὰ στόματος Δαυὶδ περὶ Ἰούδα τοῦ γενομένου ὁδηγοῦ τοῖς συλλαβοῦσιν Ἰησοῦν, ὅτι κατηριθμημένος ἦν ἐν ἡμῖν καὶ ἔλαχεν τὸν κλῆρον τῆς διακονίας ταύτης.
records.gloss: Men brothers, it was necessary to be fulfilled the Scripture which spoke beforehand the Spirit the Holy through mouth of David concerning Judas, the [one] having become guide to those having seized Jesus, \v 17 for numbered he was among us and obtained the share of the ministry this.
pieces: "{{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, what the Holy Spirit foretold in Scripture by the mouth of David had to come true. He spoke about Judas, who led the way for those who seized Jesus.
Judas was counted as one of us, and this ministry was given to him as his portion.

L.16: "Men, brothers, it was necessary for the Scripture to be fulfilled which the Holy Spirit spoke beforehand through [the] mouth of David concerning Judas, who became a guide to those who seized Jesus,
L.17: for he was numbered among us and obtained the share of this ministry.

R.16: "My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, long ago the Holy Spirit spoke through King David in the Scriptures. He told what would happen to Judas, the man who showed the way to the people who arrested Jesus. Those words had to come true.
R.17: Judas was one of our group, and he had his part in the work we do.

decisions.choice: men, brothers: a formal way to address an assembly
decisions.reason: Speakers in Acts use this form to open a speech (2:29, 13:26, 15:7). Peter is speaking to the 120, women among them (1:14-15). Whether the formula took in the women, or Peter turns here to the men because only a man may be chosen (1:21), cannot be settled from the words.

decisions.choice: it was necessary: it had to happen, because God had said it would
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word for what God has purposed and Scripture foretold (Luke 24:26, 24:44).

decisions.choice: the Scripture spoken through David: the psalms quoted in 1:20
decisions.reason: Psalms 69 and 109 carry David's name in their headings. The Holy Spirit speaks through the human writer, as in 4:25.

decisions.choice: the share: his allotted portion, the same word as "lot" in 1:26
decisions.reason: The word means a lot cast, and so the portion it gives. Judas had been given his share in the work, and by lot his place goes to another.

decisions.choice: this ministry: the service the apostles were given
decisions.reason: The word means service. In 1:25 it is paired with "apostleship"; in 6:4 the apostles speak of "the ministry of the word".

decisions.choice: brothers and sisters, with "brothers" as the alternative; Literal keeps "men, brothers"
decisions.reason: The inclusive default fits an assembly of men and women, which the meaning note marks as uncertain. Literal keeps both Greek words.

decisions.choice: long ago; King David; what would happen to
alternatives: spoke beforehand through the mouth of David concerning
decisions.reason: Readable says who David was and what "spoke beforehand" means.

records.source: Οὗτος μὲν οὖν ἐκτήσατο χωρίον ἐκ μισθοῦ τῆς ἀδικίας, καὶ πρηνὴς γενόμενος ἐλάκησεν μέσος, καὶ ἐξεχύθη πάντα τὰ σπλάγχνα αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: This [one] indeed therefore acquired a field out of [the] wages of the unrighteousness, and headlong having become he burst open in middle, and poured out all the intestines of him.
pieces: (This man came to own a field, paid for with what he earned by his crime. Falling headfirst, he split open in the middle, and all his bowels gushed out.

L.18: (Now this man acquired a field out of the reward of [his] wickedness, and falling headlong he burst open in the middle, and all his intestines poured out.

R.18: (Judas was paid money for the evil thing he did, and that money bought a field. Judas fell down headfirst, his body burst open, and all his insides poured out.

decisions.choice: 1:18-19 is an aside by Luke for his readers
decisions.reason: The 120 knew what had happened, but Luke's readers did not. Calling Aramaic "their own language" and translating the name (1:19) suits the writer, not Peter speaking in Jerusalem. The renderings put the aside in parentheses within Peter's speech, which goes on in 1:20.

decisions.choice: acquired a field: the field was bought with his money
alternatives: he bought it himself, before he died
decisions.reason: Matthew 27:3-8 tells that Judas threw the silver back and the chief priests bought a field with it. Luke speaks of it as his, since his payment bought it. Both say the field took its name from blood.

decisions.choice: falling headlong
decisions.reason: The word means "face down, headlong". An ancient medical use, "swollen", has also been proposed, but it is not well attested.

decisions.choice: Judas; the evil thing he did
decisions.reason: Readable names Judas and says what his "wickedness" was in plain words.

records.source: καὶ γνωστὸν ἐγένετο πᾶσι τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν Ἰερουσαλήμ, ὥστε κληθῆναι τὸ χωρίον ἐκεῖνο τῇ ἰδίᾳ διαλέκτῳ αὐτῶν Ἁκελδαμάχ, τοῦτ’ ἔστιν Χωρίον Αἵματος.
records.gloss: And known it became to all those dwelling in Jerusalem, so that to be called the field that in the own language of them Hakeldamach, that is, Field of Blood.
pieces: This became common knowledge among all who lived in Jerusalem, and so that piece of land came to be known in their own language as Hakeldama, which means Field of Blood.)

L.19: And it became known to all those living in Jerusalem, so that that field was called in their own language Hakeldamach, that is, Field of Blood.)

R.19: All the people in Jerusalem found out about this. So they named that field Hakeldama. In their language this means Field of Blood.)

decisions.choice: their own language: Aramaic, the everyday language of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The name is Aramaic. Luke writes in Greek and translates it for his readers.

decisions.choice: Field of Blood: named for the blood of Judas's death
alternatives: named for the blood money that bought it
decisions.reason: Luke links the name to Judas's death there. Matthew 27:6-8 links it to the price of blood. The name fits both.

decisions.choice: Hakeldamach (L); Hakeldama (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal spells the name as the Greek has it, with the opening h-sound and the final letter. Balanced and Readable drop the final letter, which Greek adds to the Aramaic name.

records.source: γέγραπται γὰρ ἐν βίβλῳ ψαλμῶν· Γενηθήτω ἡ ἔπαυλις αὐτοῦ ἔρημος καὶ μὴ ἔστω ὁ κατοικῶν ἐν αὐτῇ, καί· Τὴν ἐπισκοπὴν αὐτοῦ λαβέτω ἕτερος.
records.gloss: It has been written for in [the] book of Psalms: Let become the homestead of him desolate and not let there be the [one] dwelling in it, and: The office of him let take another.
pieces: For it is written in the book of Psalms, 'May his home become a ruin, with no one living in it,' and, 'Let someone else take over his post.'

L.20: For it has been written in [the] book of Psalms, 'Let his homestead become desolate, and let there be no one living in it,' and, 'Let another take his office.'

R.20: This is what is written in the book of Psalms: 'Let his house be empty. Let no one live in it.' It also says, 'Let someone else take over his work as a leader.'

decisions.choice: Psalm 69:26, applied to Judas
decisions.reason: The psalm prays against the enemies of the righteous sufferer, and speaks of "their" camp. Peter makes it singular and applies it to Judas, the betrayer of the righteous one. The Gospels apply Psalm 69 to Jesus's suffering (John 2:17, 15:25; Matthew 27:34).

decisions.choice: Psalm 109:8: another is to take his office
decisions.reason: The psalm is a prayer against a false friend who repays love with hatred (109:4-5). Peter draws from it that Judas's place must be filled.

decisions.choice: his office: his post, his task of oversight
decisions.reason: The word means oversight, and so the position of one who oversees. Here it is Judas's place among the Twelve. The word later gave "bishop", but that office is not meant here.

decisions.choice: homestead: his dwelling place
decisions.reason: The word means a country house or dwelling. Here it may also point to the field of 1:18-19.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks for the psalms
decisions.reason: Peter's speech is already a quotation, so the psalms he quotes take single marks.

records.source: δεῖ οὖν τῶν συνελθόντων ἡμῖν ἀνδρῶν ἐν παντὶ χρόνῳ ᾧ εἰσῆλθεν καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς, ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τοῦ βαπτίσματος Ἰωάννου ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ἧς ἀνελήμφθη ἀφ’ ἡμῶν, μάρτυρα τῆς ἀναστάσεως αὐτοῦ σὺν ἡμῖν γενέσθαι ἕνα τούτων.
records.gloss: It is necessary therefore of the having accompanied us men in all [the] time in which went in and went out among us the Lord Jesus, \v 22 having begun from the baptism of John until the day in which he was taken up from us, a witness of the resurrection of him with us to become one of these.
pieces: So we need one of the men who kept company with us all through the time the Lord Jesus came and went among us,
from the day John baptized up to the day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was taken from us. One of these must join us as a witness to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} resurrection."

L.21: So it is necessary that of the men who have accompanied us during all the time [in] which the Lord Jesus went in and went out among us,
L.22: beginning from the baptism of John until the day [on] which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was taken up from us, one of these become a witness with us of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} resurrection."

R.21: So we must choose a man to join us. He must be someone who was with us the whole time the Lord Jesus traveled with us.
R.22: That time began when John was baptizing people. It ended on the day Jesus was taken up from us into heaven. This man must be someone who can tell people, as we do, that Jesus came back to life."

decisions.choice: went in and went out among us: lived and worked among us, day by day
decisions.reason: The phrase is a Hebrew way of speaking of a person's whole life and work (Numbers 27:17, Deuteronomy 31:2, 1 Samuel 18:16).

decisions.choice: from the baptism of John: from the time John was baptizing, when Jesus's work began
decisions.reason: Jesus was baptized by John and then began his work (Luke 3:21-23). Peter uses the same starting point in 10:37.

decisions.choice: a witness of his resurrection: the center of the apostles' task
decisions.reason: What the apostles testify above all is that God raised Jesus (2:32, 3:15, 4:33). To do this one must have known him before and after.

decisions.choice: men: the word is male
decisions.reason: Peter uses the word for men, not the general word for people. So the one chosen is to be a man, like the Twelve.

decisions.choice: we must choose; into heaven
alternatives: it is necessary; he was taken up from us
decisions.reason: Readable says what "it is necessary" leads to (1:23-26) and where Jesus was taken.

records.source: καὶ ἔστησαν δύο, Ἰωσὴφ τὸν καλούμενον Βαρσαββᾶν, ὃς ἐπεκλήθη Ἰοῦστος, καὶ Μαθθίαν.
records.gloss: And they put forward two, Joseph the [one] called Barsabbas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias.
pieces: They proposed two men, Joseph who was called Barsabbas and was also known as Justus, and Matthias.

L.23: And they put forward two, Joseph, called Barsabbas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias.

R.23: The group named two men. One was Joseph, who was called Barsabbas. His other name was Justus. The other man was Matthias.

decisions.choice: they: the whole group, or the apostles, put the two forward
decisions.reason: The subject is not named. The group puts forward candidates, and God makes the choice (1:24).

decisions.choice: Joseph had an Aramaic name, Barsabbas, and a Latin one, Justus
decisions.reason: "Bar" is Aramaic for "son of". Jews of the time often had a Greek or Latin name as well (12:12, 13:9).

decisions.choice: the group named
decisions.reason: Readable avoids "chose", since the choice is God's in 1:24.

records.source: καὶ προσευξάμενοι εἶπαν Σὺ κύριε καρδιογνῶστα πάντων, ἀνάδειξον ὃν ἐξελέξω, ἐκ τούτων τῶν δύο ἕνα, λαβεῖν τὸν τόπον τῆς διακονίας ταύτης καὶ ἀποστολῆς, ἀφ’ ἧς παρέβη Ἰούδας πορευθῆναι εἰς τὸν τόπον τὸν ἴδιον.
records.gloss: And having prayed they said, You Lord, knower of hearts of all, show which you chose of these the two one \v 25 to take the place of the ministry this and apostleship, from which turned aside Judas to go to the place the own.
pieces: And they prayed, "Lord, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who know the hearts of all people, make plain which one of these two is {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} choice
to fill the place in this ministry and apostleship that Judas deserted to go to his own place."

L.24: And having prayed, they said, "You, Lord, knower of the hearts of all, show which one of these two {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have chosen
L.25: to take the place of this ministry and apostleship, from which Judas turned aside to go to his own place."

R.24: Then they prayed, "Lord, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know what is in everyone's heart. Show us which of these two men {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have chosen.
R.25: Judas turned away from his work as an apostle and went where he belonged. Show us the one who will take his place in this work."

decisions.choice: Lord: Jesus, who chose the apostles
decisions.reason: Jesus chose the first apostles (1:2, Luke 6:13), and "the Lord Jesus" has just been named (1:21). But in 15:7-8 it is God who chooses and "knows the heart", so the prayer may be to God.

decisions.choice: knower of the hearts of all: one who sees what is inside everyone
alternatives: a judge of words and deeds only
decisions.reason: The same word is used of God in 15:8; compare 1 Samuel 16:7, "the LORD looks on the heart".

decisions.choice: to go to his own place: to the end that fit what he did
decisions.reason: The words play on "place": Judas left his place among the apostles for a place of his own. They likely mean his death and judgment, but they say it with restraint.

decisions.choice: this ministry and apostleship: the service of being an apostle
decisions.reason: The two words name one task together: the service of those sent out by Jesus.

decisions.choice: Readable puts Judas's leaving first, then repeats the request
decisions.reason: The Greek clause about Judas hangs on "place"; Readable makes it a sentence of its own.

records.source: καὶ ἔδωκαν κλήρους αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἔπεσεν ὁ κλῆρος ἐπὶ Μαθθίαν, καὶ συγκατεψηφίσθη μετὰ τῶν ἕνδεκα ἀποστόλων.
records.gloss: And they gave lots for them, and fell the lot on Matthias, and he was counted together with the eleven apostles.
pieces: They drew lots for the two, the lot fell on Matthias, and from then on he was counted with the eleven apostles.

L.26: And they gave lots for them, and the lot fell on Matthias, and he was counted together with the eleven apostles.

R.26: Then they used lots to decide between the two men. The lot showed that Matthias was the one. So Matthias became an apostle along with the other eleven.

decisions.choice: casting lots: marked stones were shaken until one fell out
decisions.reason: Israel used lots to learn God's will (Leviticus 16:8, Joshua 18:6); "the lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD" (Proverbs 16:33). Acts does not tell of lots being used again.

decisions.choice: was counted together with: added to their number
alternatives: was voted in by the group
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for a voting pebble, but the choice was made by lot. It means he was reckoned among the apostles, making twelve again.

decisions.choice: they gave lots for them: lots were cast for the two
alternatives: they gave lots to the two men to draw
decisions.reason: "For them" may mean on their behalf; each man's name may have been marked on a stone.

decisions.choice: drew lots
decisions.reason: "Drew lots" is how English says it; Literal keeps "gave".

decisions.choice: became an apostle along with the other eleven
alternatives: was counted with the eleven apostles
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what being counted with them meant.
